Per-year directories follow the pattern /hc3/bospre/<year> (home), /hc3/bospre/<year>/pre_contest_index.html and /hc3/bospre/<year>/scoreboard.web.pdf; search also listed 2007, 2009, 2011, 2015 scoreboards and a 2015 Bridgewater State host page (https://webhost.bridgew.edu/jsantore/BOSPRE2015.html) — capture the whole tree now. nena-atlantic (Science Atlantic / APICS): https://scienceatlantic.ca/committees/compsci/icpc/ is a one-stop results list for every Atlantic preliminary 1998-2025 (winners + members); https://web.cs.dal.ca/~dpc/atlantic.html gives host/date/site URLs 2005-2014; Science Atlantic annual reports (PDF) carry the podium each year. NZPC: the real official site is https://nzprogcontest.org.nz/ (nzpc.org.nz is an unrelated organisation); its results archive covers 2015-2026 only (per-year /results/<year>/, scoreboards /Scoreboards/<year>/WinningTeams<year>.html, problem sets /ProblemSets/NZPC_<year>.pdf). Pre-2015 history lives on the old Otago-hosted site http://www.cs.otago.ac.nz/PC/nzcontest/history.html (robots-blocked for WebFetch; web.archive.org page fetches are SITE_BLOCKED in this environment) and on Dinneen's Auckland pages (only nz00results.html exists). SPCPA archive https://sppcontests.org/archive/<year>-icpc-results/ (1991-2024) carries the South Pacific regional with NZ site reports and often names the NZ champions — useful for the south-pacific-* parents. Phil Robbins (NZPC director 2004-2026) died in 2026; Chris Handley (Otago) was NZ Contest Director around 2000-2003. ICPC Caribbean: https://www.icpccaribe.org/ (Google Sites) is the official hub: 'Podios de los Concursos Regionales Caribeños' lists every Caribbean Final with date, podium, ranking PDF (Google Drive) and icpc.global finder slugs (caribfinals-<season>); 'Clasificados Regional <year>' (2020-2024) and 'Resultados Equipos Preuniversitarios <year>' (2017-2024) cover the Eliminatoria/Qualifier; the qualifiers since 2020 run on MatcomGrader (contest ids 6259 = 2020, 6262 = 2021; titles match the catalogue names exactly). UCLV's DMOJ blog (https://dmoj.uclv.cu/blog/5, 2019 Cuban site report) and UCI news cover earlier editions; social channels: @icpc_caribe, facebook.com/icpc.caribbean.media, YouTube channel UCehXgKiLasq-9WMOkDnQ9ng, campcarib.wordpress.com.
